A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same CTRL research. The main text and Appendices A-E, including equations, figures, tables, and examples, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-generation and critic-evaluation experiments, simulations, and supplementary analyses, including Tables 1-5 and Figures 3-7 and 10.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results, simulations, and supplementary analyses. Their retention from v1 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Both versions use execution-guided critique synthesis, supervised finetuning, GRPO, and the same iterative critique-revision procedure. The corrected equations align with the procedure already described in v1; they do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both train on filtered TACO and evaluate on CodeContests, LiveCodeBench (24.08-24.11), MBPP+, and JudgeBench. No represented tasks, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1-4 and Figure 6, including execution feedback, self-critique, the SFT critic, GPT-4o, and the JudgeBench comparison models. The new related-work citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same training data selection, model configurations, metrics, and evaluation procedures, including temperature 0.7 for initial solutions and critiques, greedy revisions, and the 1,024-token inference limit.

E4.justification: The difficulty, model-size, error-compounding, code-similarity, and timeout analyses are unchanged. Appendices C-E retain the majority-voting analysis, PPO value-network instability evidence, and the same critique examples.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averages in Table 3 and standard-error bands in Figures 1 and 4. The simulation repetition details and other statistical reporting practices are also unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are retained throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 reports the same CodeContests Pass@1 values of 7.88% for zero-shot Qwen2.5-Coder and 16.24% after five CTRL critique-revision rounds.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the policy-gradient conditioning to z = (x, y') and makes the GRPO sampling distribution, probability ratios, and KL terms refer to critiques c_i conditioned on z, replacing inconsistent terms such as Q_theta(y_i | x). These are limited mathematical corrections beyond the Q-to-C notation change; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: training critics without human supervision, guiding stronger generators, improving discrimination, and enabling iterative test-time scaling. The headline improvement claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of reduced error compounding, broader revisions, cross-domain generalization, and the accuracy-versus-runtime tradeoff are retained. The conclusion identifies the same future directions concerning efficiency, safety, and multi-turn training.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same prompts, hint templates, data-cleaning instructions, VeRL training details, and SFT/RL hyperparameters in Tables 8-9. The project link and SandboxFusion disclosure are unchanged; the latter merely moves with text reflow.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds self-reflection and cites Feng et al. (2024), Natural Language Reinforcement Learning. The additional Shinn et al. (2023) reference describes the already cited Reflexion work. The broader research positioning and Appendix B comparison remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 renames the critic notation from Q_theta to C_theta, fixes several grammatical and punctuation errors, and changes appendix cross-reference wording to 'Section'. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conference proceedings and copyright block on the first page and reflows text and equations across columns and pages. The existing figures, table structures, and captions are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The Section 3.3 corrections remove inconsistent conditioning and action variables from the displayed optimization equations, improving mathematical clarity and consistency with the stated method. Small editorial and related-work updates provide additional limited benefits. The empirical evidence and scientific scope remain unchanged.
